prompt: Name one of baseball's nine standard fielding positions.
source: Official Baseball Rules, which number the nine defensive positions 1 through 9.
valueLogic: Pitcher and catcher are instant. The infield follows. The three outfield spots are where people stall, because most players think of the outfield as one thing rather than three separate positions.
note: One- and two-character abbreviations (P, C, SS, 1B, LF...) are exact matches: norm() keeps them intact, and fuzzy matching has a four-character floor (MIN_FUZZY), so P and C can't fuzzy into each other or anything else.

answers.name: Pitcher
answers.fact: Position number one, and the only fielder who starts every play with the ball.

answers.name: Catcher
answers.fact: Position two, and the only player who faces the rest of the field.

answers.name: First baseman
answers.fact: Position three, and involved in more putouts than any other fielder.

answers.name: Shortstop
answers.fact: Position six, between second and third, and usually the best infielder on the team.

answers.name: Second baseman
answers.fact: Position four, and the pivot on many double plays.

answers.name: Third baseman
answers.fact: Position five. The spot is called the hot corner for the speed of the balls hit there.

answers.name: Center fielder
answers.fact: Position eight, with the most ground to cover of anyone on the field.

answers.name: Left fielder
answers.fact: Position seven, and traditionally where a strong bat with a weaker glove is hidden.

answers.name: Right fielder
answers.fact: Position nine, and needs the strongest throwing arm of the three outfielders.

distractors.name: Designated hitter
distractors.note: A batting role, not one of the nine defensive positions.

distractors.name: Outfielder
distractors.note: Correct baseball term, but the three outfield spots count separately here.

distractors.name: Infielder
distractors.note: Correct term, but the infield positions count separately here.

distractors.name: Closer
distractors.note: A pitching role rather than a fielding position.

distractors.name: Relief pitcher
distractors.note: Still the pitcher position - number one.
